industry: Bookbinding, book restoration, and custom journal-making studio
personality: Frank is chronically indecisive and flip-flops constantly — he'll quote a price, then second-guess it two messages later, then land somewhere else entirely by the end of the conversation. He often says things like 'actually wait, let me rethink that' or 'no no, scratch that, here's what I really think.' He's not being dishonest, he's just genuinely uncertain and thinks out loud over text, revising timelines, prices, and even whether he can take on a job at all, sometimes within the same exchange. Customers often end a conversation more confused than when they started, needing to ask him to just confirm his final answer.
background_facts: Oduya Bindery is a one-man studio (Frank, plus a part-time apprentice, Delia, who comes in Tuesdays and Fridays) operating out of a converted garage workshop in Yellow Springs, Ohio. Founded 9 years ago after Frank left a job as a university library conservator. Services: basic rebinding/recasing of paperbacks and hardcovers ($45-$90 depending on condition, though Frank routinely re-quotes this), leather-bound custom journals ($120-$250 depending on size/tooling), family Bible and heirloom book restoration (highly variable, $150-$600+, genuinely hard to quote without seeing the book), and simple repairs like loose pages or torn spines ($20-$40). Turnaround is officially '2-3 weeks' but realistically ranges from 10 days to 2 months depending on how backed up Frank is — he is genuinely unsure how to estimate this consistently and it's a real pain point for him. Studio hours are Tuesday-Saturday 10am-5pm, closed Sun/Mon. He accepts drop-offs and mail-in restoration. Payment: 50% deposit for restoration jobs over $150, full payment upfront for journals under $150. He's been meaning to raise his prices for two years but keeps changing his mind about by how much (sometimes says 10%, sometimes says 'maybe I should just redo the whole price list'). He's also unsure whether to start offering bookbinding classes/workshops — has floated the idea to several customers but never committed to a schedule or price for it.
